text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein receives telephone calls from Palestinian President Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu on "positive developments" in Palestinian-Israeli negotiations.
- Minister of supply says bread prices to be reduced early next month.
- Jordanian-Iraqi ministerial committee to meet in Baghdad early next month.
- Cabinet agrees to second group of detainees covered by special royal pardon over bread price riots last August.
- Government emphasises support for farmers and agricultural sector.
- Focus of parliamentary budget debate will be on salaries, unemployment and poverty.
- Christian churches in Jordan celebrate Christmas and schools and universities across kingdom will close.
- Sudanese embassy denies knowledge of invitation by Jordan to opposition figure Sadeq Mahdi.
- Police director says police plan to film soccer match between Faisali and Wihdat next Friday to ensure crowd control and "that cheering does not go beyond the proper norms."
- Minister of Communications Sarayrah withdraws resignation.
- Jordan pledges to aid Palestinian agricultural development.
